clue.text: 6 1dn's image first during break

indicators.note: during says the next pieces fall within the span of the break

parts.note: HOL is the usual short form of holiday, a break
the spit, as in the spitting image, is an exact likeness
A, as in A1 or grade A, stands for first-class

explanation.surface: The National Health's public image comes first, even while it takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 1dn is NATIONAL HEALTH, so the definition is something belonging to the National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A typical institution run by Britain's National Health Service is a place where the sick are treated.

clue.text: See 6
In poor 1dn when the King and I swap an island

indicators.text: when the King and I swap
indicators.note: the King (K, the chess and card abbreviation) takes the place of I in the island's name

parts.note: Sicily is the large Italian island off the toe of Italy

explanation.surface: Someone in poor health thinks of The King and I while an island is exchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 1dn is HEALTH, so 'In poor 1dn' reads 'in poor health'. The surface nods at the musical The King and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is often ill or ailing is described as weak and frail, the condition of poor health.

clue.text: Painfully treat 10 on the other side

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: ten written as a figure looks like the letters I and O

indicators.note: the other side means a different version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to give number ten some painful treatment on the opposite flank.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10-across, but here it is just the figures read as letters. 'the other' turns SIDE into DISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a wound with iodine is a familiar stinging, painful remedy, hence painful treatment.

clue.text: Hardly any use concealing what Santa says in Northamptonshire mansion

indicators.note: concealing says the outer letters hide another piece within them
hardly suggests a poor, barely recognisable version, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Father Christmas traditionally booms 'ho ho'

explanation.surface: A Northamptonshire stately home is said to be almost useless while hiding Father Christmas's laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly' rearranges the letters of 'any', and 'concealing' hides Santa's laugh between that and USE. Northamptonshire is an English Midlands county, and Aynho is a village in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aynho House, also called Aynho Park, is a country house in the village of Aynho in Northamptonshire.

clue.text: Infant rumoured to be a hole in the head

indicators.note: to be says these letters are to become the answer, sitting within the words before

explanation.surface: Gossip that a baby has a hole in its head.
explanation.definitionFit: An antrum is an anatomical cavity, especially a sinus in the skull bones, so literally a hole in the head.

clue.text: Race to heal disease and halt corruption in the service

parts.note: a nation is a people or race

indicators.note: disease suggests something disordered, so the letters before it are jumbled
corruption means spoiling or distorting, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: A race to cure illness and stop corruption within the public service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disease' rearranges HEAL to ALHE and 'corruption' rearranges HALT to ALTH, so the two anagrams together make the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's state medical system is formally the National Health Service, commonly called simply the service by those within it.

clue.text: Problem with 5? It is sequential to a cut flower

indicators.note: sequential to says the next piece comes after, following in order
cut says the river's name is docked of its final letter

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Rhine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical problem that follows on from cutting a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword shorthand for a river. 5 is ANTRUM, a sinus cavity, so the problem is one of the nose and sinuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the nasal lining, near the sinus cavities, is a typical ailment affecting that part of the head.

clue.text: Alberta hat for 1dn?

parts.note: a city in Alberta, Canada, is named with a word plus Hat, and that first word is also something taken for health

explanation.surface: A Canadian hat that is good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: Medicine Hat is a city in Alberta, Canada; 1dn is HEALTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs or remedies are what a patient takes to restore good health, so they are for health.

clue.text: Emergency partner for police coming into a little money

indicators.note: coming into says one piece enters another and sits inside it

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: Detectives arrive to collect a small sum in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: A hospital's casualty department in Britain is called Accident and Emergency, so the answer is Emergency's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: British hospitals pair the two words in the casualty unit's name, Accident and Emergency, often written A&E.

clue.text: Riding hat not hard on Dame Thora

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out of the word before it

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
Dame Thora Hird was a much-loved English actress

explanation.surface: A riding hat that is not a hard hat, worn by an elderly actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riding' looks like horse riding; it is one of the Ridings of Yorkshire, an old English county whose three divisions took their name from 'thriding', a third part.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire was split into three Ridings, each name coming from an Old Norse word for a third part.

clue.text: Break in 1ac task ruined when people start to discuss work

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: HOL, short for holiday, is the break used in the 1ac clue

indicators.note: start says only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: During a hospital break a job falls apart when staff begin talking about their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' scrambles HOL and TASK into TALKSHO, then P comes from the start of 'people'.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk shop is an idiom meaning to chat about one's job, especially in social company.

clue.text: Reverse of 12ac in heaven

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Reverse of 12ac in heaven' refers to itself; reversing DOZ (12) gives ZOD and AC is printed, but nothing fairly supplies the I, so no honest parse of ZODIAC

clue.text: How 1ac worker and friend could be marketed?

definitions.text: How 1ac worker and friend could be marketed?

parts.note: an intern is a junior doctor working in a hospital
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A question about how a hospital employee and a companion might be sold.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to the NHS internal market of the 1990s, under which hospitals sold services to one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Within the health service's own internal market, services were bought and sold inside the organisation, that is, from within.

clue.text: Top 1ac? If not, do an U-turn

indicators.note: the turn in U-turn says the letters around it turn into a new order

explanation.surface: If the top hospital is not what you wanted, make a U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder takes the U from U-turn; 'turn' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Foundation hospitals were the top-rated NHS trusts given extra independence from 2004, so a leading hospital.

clue.text: Ambivalent model stuck without love

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: wedged means jammed tight, stuck
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A model who is stuck without a lover feels ambivalent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, putting WEDGED around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something double-edged cuts both ways, so an ambivalent remark has two contrasting meanings.

clue.text: Break time during renderings of brother priest

parts.note: Fra is the Italian title for a friar or brother

indicators.note: during says one piece falls within the span of another

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A break while a monk and a priest each give their renderings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renderings of' says the words for brother and priest are translated, Italian FRA and French CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracture is a break, especially in a bone, which fits the hospital theme.

clue.text: 8 good for the ambitious?

parts.note: 8 is MEDICINE, and aspirin is an example of one

explanation.surface: A suggestion that medicine is good for people with ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is MEDICINE; aspirin is an everyday medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aspiring hopes to rise or achieve something, which is what ambitious people do.

clue.text: 1ac's local authority is prodigal: holding back is the 8 man

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a prodigal spends recklessly, a waster

indicators.note: back means the pair of pieces next to it read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
8 is MEDICINE, and its man is a doctor, abbreviated DR

explanation.surface: A hospital's local council is wasteful, and the doctor is holding back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives RDSI, the doctor and 'is' read backwards. The first 'is' is only a link word; the definition means the person in charge of a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior nurse in charge of a hospital ward is the person in authority on that ward.

clue.text: Some insect studies at B-Bury?

indicators.note: some means only part of the word is used, its ending docked

parts.note: entomology is the scientific study of insects
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bit of insect research done at the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B-Bury' gives the letter B and then the definition, Bury, which poses as the Lancashire town.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb, a way to bury it.

clue.text: Reactionary scientist starting reactionary book on gas?

indicators.note: reactionary is read as going backwards, so the pieces are turned round

parts.note: VOL is the abbreviation for volume, a book

indicators.note: starting means only the opening part of the word for gas is kept

parts.note: vapour is a gas

explanation.surface: A right-wing scientist begins a backward-looking book about gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reactionary' turns VOL plus VAP into PAVLOV. Pavlov studied conditioned reactions, hence the reactionary scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Pavlov was the Russian physiologist famous for studying conditioned reflexes, or reactions, in dogs.

clue.text: Dead ringer for Blake?

definitions.meaning: a church officer who tolls the bell for the dead and digs graves
the first name of the fictional detective Blake of boys' stories

explanation.definitionFit: A church sexton rings bells and digs graves; Sexton Blake was a popular British fictional detective.

clue.text: Prompter's back cover of "Elements"

indicators.note: back means the word before it is read in reverse

parts.note: a cue is the prompter's signal to an actor
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: The back cover of a book called Elements, by way of a prompter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CUE into EUC. The definition is the author of Elements.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek mathematician Euclid wrote the Elements, the classic treatise on geometry.

clue.text: Part of 25 is one part of 18: when?

parts.note: one as a Roman numeral is I
18 is WARD SISTER, and a sister is also a nun
a date says when something happens

explanation.surface: A question of when one piece of one entry joins another.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is FLOODLIT, whose first part is FLOOD; 18 is WARD SISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood something is to inundate it, overwhelming it with water.

clue.text: Servant of one being married, say, (to Kate) my first love?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a groom is a man on his wedding day
I is the first-person word for oneself
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A servant of a bridegroom wed to Kate, perhaps a first love.
explanation.walkthrough: Grumio is Petruchio's servant in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, in which Petruchio marries Kate; '(to Kate)' sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumio is the comic servant of Petruchio in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Lots of lots during getaway exposed

indicators.note: during says one piece falls within the span of another

parts.note: a flit is a hasty escape, especially a moonlight flit

indicators.note: lots of means most of the word, so its ending is docked

parts.note: oodles means lots

explanation.surface: Plenty of goods carried off during an escape are exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots of' docks the last two letters of the word for lots, a loose Araucaria-style truncation signal; a flit, as in a moonlight flit, is a secret getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something floodlit is lit up brightly by lamps, so exposed to view.

clue.text: Scrape the bottom of 1 in 100 generally

indicators.note: 1 in says one word sits inside the words that follow, the rest of them discarded

parts.note: the figure 100 is written out as the word hundred, followed by generally as printed

explanation.surface: Scrape the bottom of the barrel, as one does in a hundred cases in general.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 100 out in words: the answer is the run inside HUNDRED GENERALLY, with HUN at the front and NERALLY at the back thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge a river is to scrape mud up from its bed.

clue.text: Principal in 14 of 6 1dn with note about the old Eastern front

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around another

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is a written note
ye is an old form of the
the van is the front of an army

explanation.surface: The founder of the National Health with a note about the old Eastern front.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is FOUNDATION and 6 1dn is NATIONAL HEALTH. Aneurin (Nye) Bevan was the minister who founded the NHS in 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: Aneurin Bevan, as Labour health minister, was the chief architect of Britain's National Health Service.
